children: shares jumped after the chipmaker sharply raised its long-term revenue outlook at its 2026 investor day, giving investors a more aggressive roadmap for how AI infrastructure demand could reshape the company over the next several years. The biggest surprise was not just the fiscal 2028 increase, but Marvell's forecast for as much as $90 billion in annual revenue by fiscal 2031.

Marvell is a data-infrastructure semiconductor company that sells custom silicon, networking, optical and connectivity products used across cloud and AI data centers. Its growth increasingly depends on hyperscalers deploying custom accelerators and high-speed interconnect technologies alongside Nvidia-based systems.

For fiscal 2028, Marvell now expects revenue of about $20 billion, up from its prior $18 billion outlook and above the $18.2 billion analyst consensus. The company also said customer revenue in fiscal 2029 could rise 200% or more.

The longer-term numbers were even more aggressive. Marvell expects total revenue to reach between $70 billion and $90 billion by fiscal 2031, implying an $80 billion midpoint that is dramatically above the roughly $46.9 billion Wall Street consensus cited by Reuters.

That forecast builds on Marvell's expanding role in custom AI silicon. The company has secured a major agreement with Alphabet's Google that could generate as much as $120 billion in revenue through 2033 if performance milestones are met.
Marvell's fiscal 2026 revenue reached $8.2 billion, up 42% year over year, while management has said AI bookings remain exceptionally strong.

The investor-day targets significantly raise the bar for execution. Investors should watch custom-silicon revenue growth, hyperscaler customer wins, AI networking demand and whether gross margins hold as the business mix shifts.

The bullish case strengthens if Marvell's Google relationship and other custom-chip programs begin scaling on schedule. The biggest risk is timing: prior investor concerns centered on how quickly those large design wins actually convert into revenue.

Fiscal 2028 therefore becomes a key checkpoint. If Marvell can approach $20 billion while maintaining healthy margins, the fiscal 2031 target will look increasingly credible. Delays in custom silicon ramps or hyperscaler spending would make the $70 billion to $90 billion ambition much harder to justify.

title: Marvell Stock Soars After Raising 2028 Guidance
